hero.eyebrow: You’re leaning right now, aren’t you?
hero.headline: Stop leaning into your screen.
hero.subhead: Holdup watches your posture through your webcam. Lean in for too long and a small Mirror of you pops up in the corner. Sit up, and it's gone.
download.macIntel: Mac with an Intel chip? Get this one
download.facts: Free · Open source · Windows, Mac and Linux · Nothing leaves your computer
download.notDesktop: Holdup is for Windows, Mac and Linux computers. Open this page on your computer to download it.
how.1.body: A quick Calibration captures your Baseline: your own good posture, not a textbook ideal.
how.1.title: Sit up once
how.2.body: Holdup sits quietly in the system tray and compares how you sit with your Baseline.
how.2.title: Work as usual
how.3.body: Lean forward or to one side for more than 5 seconds and your own picture pops up in the corner. Seeing yourself is the nudge.
how.3.title: The Mirror appears
how.4.body: Back to Good Posture and the Mirror disappears. No sounds, no pop-ups to dismiss.
how.4.title: Sit up, it's gone
how.sceneLabel: Illustration: a person at a laptop calibrates, leans toward the screen until the Mirror appears, then sits up again.
how.scrollHint: Keep scrolling to keep the animation going
how.title: How it works
privacy.body: Every camera frame is analysed in memory and thrown away. Holdup only keeps numbers, like how many minutes you sat well today, and they never leave your computer.
privacy.site: This website counts anonymous visits with GoatCounter. No cookies, nothing personal.
privacy.title: Your camera stays yours
privacy.video: The Holdup calibration screen counting down while you sit up straight
features.baseline.body: Holdup compares you with you. Moved your camera or changed chairs? It notices and asks you to Recalibrate.
features.baseline.title: Your own Baseline
features.lean.body: Catches both leaning toward the screen and tilting to one side.
features.lean.title: Forward and Side Lean
features.pause.body: Stretching, eating, in a meeting? Pause for 30 minutes, 1 hour or until you resume.
features.pause.title: Pause anytime
features.quiet.body: Lives in the tray (the menu bar on a Mac) and can start when you log in. In English and Português.
features.quiet.shot: The Today page of the Holdup app
features.quiet.title: Stays out of the way
features.sensitivity.body: Low, Medium or High: choose how far from your Baseline you may sit.
features.sensitivity.title: Sensitivity
features.stats.body: See how much of your day was Good Posture, over the last 7 or 30 days.
features.stats.shot: The History page of the Holdup app
features.stats.title: Daily Stats
features.title: Made for how you actually sit
open.body: No subscription, no account, no ads. Holdup is MIT-licensed: read every line of code on GitHub, build it yourself, or help make it better.
get.windows.1: Download HoldupSetup.exe (about 120 MB; the posture model is included so it works offline).
get.windows.2: Windows may show “Windows protected your PC”. That's normal for new apps that aren't signed yet. Click **More info**, then **Run anyway**.
get.windows.3: Install. No admin rights needed; it installs just for you.
get.done: Sit up straight for your Calibration. That's it.
get.caption: Step 2: click **Run anyway**.
get.windows.requirements: Windows 10 or 11 and a webcam (built-in or USB).
get.mac.1: Download the .dmg (about 180 MB; the posture model is included so it works offline), open it and drag Holdup into **Applications**.
get.mac.2: Open Holdup. macOS says it can't check it for malware, because it isn't signed yet. Click **Done**, then go to **System Settings → Privacy & Security** and click **Open Anyway**.
get.mac.3: Click **Allow** when macOS asks for the camera. Holdup lives in the menu bar.
get.mac.requirements: macOS 11 or later (Apple Silicon or Intel) and a webcam (built-in or USB).
get.linux.1: Download the AppImage (about 180 MB; the posture model is included so it works offline). On Ubuntu or Debian you can install the .deb instead.
get.linux.2: Make the AppImage executable: right-click it → **Properties** → **Allow executing as program**. Then open it.
get.linux.3: Look for Holdup in the system tray. On GNOME the tray needs the **AppIndicator** extension (Ubuntu has it built in).
get.linux.requirements: A 64-bit Linux desktop with a system tray (X11 or Wayland), and a webcam (built-in or USB).
get.shot: The “Windows protected your PC” dialog after clicking More info
get.title: Get Holdup
faq.calls.a: If another app takes the camera, Holdup shows Camera Unavailable and waits. You can also Pause it.
faq.free.a: Yes. MIT-licensed, no ads, no paid tier.
faq.internet.a: No. Everything runs on your computer, including the posture model.
faq.mac.a: Yes. Holdup runs on Windows 10 and 11, macOS 11 or later (Apple Silicon and Intel) and 64-bit Linux. The download button picks the right one for your computer.
faq.mac.q: Is there a Mac or Linux version?
faq.others.a: Holdup only watches the person closest to the camera: you.
faq.others.q: What if someone else walks into the frame?
faq.record.a: No. Frames are analysed in memory and discarded. No images or video are ever saved or sent.
faq.title: Questions
faq.uninstall.a: On Windows, from Settings → Apps. On a Mac, drag Holdup from Applications to the Trash. On Linux, delete the AppImage or remove the holdup package. Your Daily Stats stay on your computer until you delete them.
faq.warning.a: Windows and macOS warn about apps that aren't code-signed, which costs money every year. Holdup isn't signed yet. The code is public on GitHub, so you (or anyone) can check exactly what it does.
faq.warning.q: Why does my computer warn me when I install it?
why.author: Pablo
why.quote: I noticed I was always leaning toward the screen while working, and it started to worry me. I wanted something that would remind me to sit up without me having to remember. So I built Holdup.
why.title: Why I built Holdup
